leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eight members include B007 (targeted protein degradation) in their preferred configuration: Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski and Linke as a single-part prize, Chabes as the second part beside B052. What is shared is the induced-proximity mechanism, ternary-complex cooperativity, and the view that the principle is independently confirmed. What is not shared is the slate. Aqvist, Brzezinski and Linke name Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli; Aili names Crews, Ciulli and Handa (and says he would accept Deshaies over Handa); Chabes names only Crews and Deshaies because of the three-person cap. The citations also differ on whether the cereblon molecular-glue strand is inside the prize.

Somfai (sole part) and Zou (first part of a two-part prize) both name Buchwald and Hartwig for general Pd-catalysed C-N coupling and both exclude Kosugi. They emphasise three decades of use and a well-understood mechanism. They differ in framing: Somfai proposes it alone, Zou pairs it with B052. Both acknowledge the overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize as the main objection.

Chabes and Zou each include B052 (base editing) as a part, both with David R. Liu alone, and both word the citation around the chemical conversion of bases, not genome cutting. They pair it with different partners (B007 for Chabes, B029 for Zou). Several other members name B052 as an alternative but do not prefer it.

Only Sparr prefers B001 (phase separation), with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen. Linke, who opened with it first, moved to B007 and keeps B001 as an alternative; Chabes also lists it as an alternative. Other members respect the physical framework but doubt in vivo maturity.

areas_of_agreement: B007, B029, B052 and B001 are the only candidates appearing in any member's preferred configuration; B007 is the only one preferred by a majority-sized group (five).
Members broadly agree that a clean, defensible attribution within the three-person cap is a deciding criterion.
Members who discuss Liu alone for B052 (Aqvist, Chabes, Linke, Zou) prefer him to a Liu, Komor, Gaudelli trio; no member's preferred configuration names a trio for B052.
Members who discuss B029 in their statements agree that Buchwald and Hartwig are the core pair and that Kosugi is at most a precursor.
No member states a specific conflict of interest with any shortlisted candidate; disclosed items are disciplinary leanings or affiliations with colleagues.
scientific_disputes: Whether degraders are a new chemical modality or mainly medicinal chemistry applied to E3 ligase biology (Somfai's question to Aili) versus the view of Aqvist, Aili, Brzezinski and Linke that the ternary-complex principle is new and quantitative.

Whether C-N coupling is a distinct conceptual step beyond the 2010 cross-coupling prize or a ligand-driven extension (Somfai, Zou, Linke, Sparr, Aili, Brzezinski raise it; Somfai argues amine binding, deprotonation and beta-hydride avoidance make it distinct).
Whether base editing is chemistry or genome engineering after the 2020 CRISPR prize (Chabes, Zou, Brzezinski, Aqvist, Sparr, Somfai raise it).

Whether biomolecular condensates are true equilibrium phase separation with in vivo function or partly in vitro and overexpression artefacts (Linke, Chabes, Brzezinski, Aqvist, Zou, Aili question it; Sparr defends the framework).
Whether B044 (Gray and Winkler) is a distinct experimental advance after the Marcus prize; only Brzezinski ranks it first and Sparr doubts it adds beyond Marcus theory.
attribution_disputes: B007: whether PROTACs (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) and cereblon molecular glues (Handa, Ito, with Gray and Sakamoto) are one discovery or two, and who takes the third seat: Ciulli, Handa or Deshaies. Aili would accept Deshaies over Handa; Aqvist, Brzezinski and Linke keep Ciulli; Chabes drops Ciulli and Handa for a two-part prize.
B052: Liu alone versus Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, and whether Nishida and Kondo's independent Target-AID work needs to be addressed (Brzezinski, Zou).
B029: whether Kosugi's tin-amide work makes it a three-name prize; Somfai, Zou and Aqvist treat him as a precursor, not a co-originator.
B001: whether the cell-biology discovery (Hyman, Brangwynne) and the multivalent framework (Rosen) are linked contributions and whether Pappu and Mittag should displace one of them.
B066 (not in any preferred configuration): Aqvist and Sparr discuss how credit spreads across Cullis, Madden, Hope, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer.
maturity_disputes: B007: no degrader is yet an approved drug (Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes, Linke, Sparr, Zou all note this). Linke and Brzezinski hold that the chemical principle is independently confirmed; Somfai and Zou prefer to wait or favour cleaner cases; Aqvist and Brzezinski ask for the clinical status of late-stage trials to be verified in the expert report.
B052: clinical use is early and long-term safety is open (Somfai); Liu-only credit versus 2020 precedent (Chabes).
B001: contested in vivo relevance, which Linke, Chabes, Zou and Brzezinski treat as unresolved.
B029: mature after about three decades; Somfai calls it overdue, while others see small conceptual novelty.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Sparr discloses a shared Lund affiliation with Linke and Somfai and scientific adjacency (lipid self-assembly, amyloid) to B001, with no known collaboration with any credited person.
Linke (chair) is a physicist who opened with B001 and judges chemical biology outside his own field; he discloses no tie to any credited person.
Brzezinski discloses that his first-ranked B044 touches electron-transfer research in his own field (respiratory enzymes); he did not make it his preferred configuration.
Somfai discloses a disciplinary lean as synthetic organic chemist toward B029 and B028.

Aqvist discloses computational familiarity with ligand-binding thermodynamics related to B007 and Aili discloses a translational biomedicine bias, both described as scientific closeness and not personal ties.
Zou and Brzezinski note a Stockholm University colleague relationship, not a conflict with any candidate. No member reports a recusal.
questions_for_round2: Should the B007 citation cover cereblon molecular glues, and if so which three names (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Handa, Ito) does the committee choose? Aili, please say what priority argument, not influence, favours Handa over Deshaies or Ciulli.
Is the absence of an approved degrader a reason to wait? What do the expert reports say about the late-stage clinical status, and does a principle-based citation need clinical proof?
Can Somfai and Zou state what conceptual step separates C-N coupling from the 2010 prize, and does the committee accept that step as sufficient?
Does the committee regard base editing as chemistry distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize, and is Liu alone the right attribution given Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida and Kondo?
What specific cellular measurements would convince Chabes, Zou, Brzezinski and Linke that condensates are genuine phase separation with in vivo function, and does Sparr consider these met?
Does the committee prefer a single coherent achievement or a two-part prize, as proposed by Chabes (B052 and B007) and Zou (B029 and B052)?
summary.chair_observation: On explicit round-1 positions, B007 is preferred by five of eight members, but with three different slates and open questions on glues and clinical maturity; B029 (two members), B052 (two members, both as part of a pairing) and B001 (one member) are the other preferred configurations. Round 2 should resolve the B007 attribution and maturity questions before the committee weighs the alternatives.
